item.research_question: Can a high-throughput technique be developed for combinatorial compositional design and rapid synthesis of ultrafine multimetallic nanoclusters with a homogeneous alloy structure?
item.processing_route: Thermal shock heating (∼1,650 K, ∼500 ms) of precursor-loaded carbon support
item.test_conditions: Electrochemical screening using scanning droplet cell and rotating disk electrode setup in 0.1 M KOH and 1 M KOH
key_findings: Ultrafine and homogeneous alloy MMNCs can be synthesized using thermal shock heating
The MMNCs exhibit a single-phase FCC structure
Two promising catalysts (PtPdRhNi and PtPdFeCoNi) were identified and verified using RDE setup
The MMNCs show higher activity and stability compared to Pt control sample
The high-throughput synthesis and screening method can accelerate compositional exploration for MMNC study
item.mechanism: The high-temperature synthesis in the multielement samples with a high entropy largely drives the alloy formation
item.limitations: The complexity of multielement systems limits the interpretation of the high performance of the two compositions
item.future_work: Data mining and machine learning can be used to uncover the hidden relationships on the elemental contributions to the catalytic performances
quotes: High-throughput, combinatorial synthesis of multimetallic nanoclusters
The high-throughput synthesis and screening pipeline demonstrated in this work can continuously provide valuable data for future data mining and machine learning
The uniformity of the MMNCs enables their comparative study for catalytic applications

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can a high-throughput technique be developed for combinatorial compositional design and rapid synthesis of ultrafine multimetallic nanoclusters with a homogeneous alloy structure?. System: PtPdRhRuIrFeCoNi. Processing: Thermal shock heating (∼1,650 K, ∼500 ms) of precursor-loaded carbon support. Test conditions: Electrochemical screening using scanning droplet cell and rotating disk electrode setup in 0.1 M KOH and 1 M KOH. Findings: Ultrafine and homogeneous alloy MMNCs can be synthesized using thermal shock heating; The MMNCs exhibit a single-phase FCC structure; Two promising catalysts (PtPdRhNi and PtPdFeCoNi) were identified and verified using RDE setup; The MMNCs show higher activity and stability compared to Pt control sample; The high-throughput synthesis and screening method can accelerate compositional exploration for MMNC study. Mechanism: The high-temperature synthesis in the multielement samples with a high entropy largely drives the alloy formation. Limitations: The complexity of multielement systems limits the interpretation of the high performance of the two compositions. Future work: Data mining and machine learning can be used to uncover the hidden relationships on the elemental contributions to the catalytic performances. Quote: "High-throughput, combinatorial synthesis of multimetallic nanoclusters"
